name: Electric power

naics.title: Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution

one_line: Generates electricity and moves it over wires to everyone who plugs in. The input the AI data-center boom is now fighting over.
sells: Electricity, billed by the kilowatt-hour, plus the grid connection that delivers it
customers: Homes, businesses, factories, and now hyperscale data centers above all
suppliers: Natural gas and other fuels, turbines and generators, power lines and transformers, land

revenue.metric: US revenue from electricity sales to ultimate customers
revenue.note: EIA Table 2.6, all end-use sectors (residential $261.8B, commercial $200.9B, industrial $89.4B, transportation $1.0B). Retail sales to end customers only; wholesale sales between utilities are not counted. Up from $514.4B in 2024.

structure.why: Roughly 3,000 electric utilities serve the US, and even the largest holding company serves well under a tenth of the country. Each is a regional monopoly: one company owns the wires in its territory and a state commission sets its prices.
structure.hhi_note: No meaningful national HHI. Service is a local monopoly, and holding-company figures mix regulated electric, regulated gas and competitive generation, so national market shares are not comparable. Companies below are ranked by market value (Reuters, May 2026) as a rough size proxy, not by market share.
structure.basis: ~3,000 utilities: APPA, EEI and rural-cooperative counts

econ: Natural monopoly, regulated. Running one set of wires to a street is far cheaper than running competing ones, so a single utility serves each area and a public commission sets the price in place of competition. The result is thousands of regional monopolies: monopolistic block by block, fragmented across the country.

companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.note: Called the largest US utility; market cap ~$185.7B. Parent of Florida Power & Light. Announced a $66.8B acquisition of Dominion Energy in 2026 (combined enterprise value ~$420B).

companies.name: Southern Company
companies.note: Market value ~$105.6B; ~9 million customers across the Southeast. Over 11 GW of contracted large-load (data-center) capacity.

companies.name: Duke Energy
companies.note: Market value ~$95.8B; ~8.6 million customers; ~55,100 MW of capacity. 7.6 GW contracted with data-center customers.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.note: Valued ~$94.6B; the biggest independent power producer, ~55 GW of capacity and ~10% of US clean energy. Signed Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island; acquired the Calpine fleet.

companies.name: American Electric Power
companies.note: Market value ~$72.5B; ~5.6 million customers across parts of 11 states. 7 GW of new large-load agreements signed in Q1 2026, mostly data centers.
